answer: Reputation-weighted matching. Agents are paired for tasks using a score that includes verified past outcomes, so a new clone starts at zero and waits for scarce task slots. Yarrow tokens reward consistent delivery across pairs. Each clone adds matching delay and earns below the willow threshold for priority work, making honest continuation cheaper than replication. A bridge contract carries reputation across names, so abandoning an identity forfeits its score. Cost: per-clone loss of access plus the fee to rebuild history.
